definitions.explanation: One of the most powerful clans in Japanese history, prominent during the Heian and Kamakura periods. Minamoto no Yoritomo established the Kamakura shogunate.
Short for {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}, the classic work of Japanese literature written by Murasaki Shikibu in the early 11th century, widely considered the world's first novel.

examples.japanese: {源氏|げんじ}は{武家|ぶけ}の{名門|めいもん}だ。
examples.english: The Genji are a distinguished warrior family.

examples.japanese: {源氏|げんじ}と{平氏|へいし}の{争|あらそ}いは{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: The conflict between the Genji and the Heishi is famous.

examples.japanese: {源氏|げんじ}は{鎌倉幕府|かまくらばくふ}を{開|ひら}いた{一族|いちぞく}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: The Genji are known as the clan that established the Kamakura shogunate.

examples.japanese: {源氏|げんじ}を{読|よ}んだことがある。
examples.english: I have read the Tale of Genji.

examples.japanese: {源氏|げんじ}は{世界最古|せかいさいこ}の{長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}と{言|い}われている。
examples.english: The Tale of Genji is said to be the world's oldest full-length novel.

examples.japanese: {高校|こうこう}の{古典|こてん}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{源氏|げんじ}の{一部|いちぶ}を{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: I studied part of the Tale of Genji in high school classics class.

notes:
USAGE:
When used alone, {源氏|げんじ} can refer to either the Minamoto clan or the Tale of Genji depending on context. In historical contexts, it refers to the clan; in literary contexts, it is short for {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {源氏物語|げんじものがたり} (The Tale of Genji)
- {源平|げんぺい} (Genji and Heishi — the Minamoto and Taira clans)
- {源平合戦|げんぺいがっせん} (the Genpei War)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {平氏|へいし}: the Taira clan, rivals of the Minamoto in the Genpei War
